question.text: Under Section 212 of the Companies Act, 2013, which of the following can trigger an SFIO investigation?

answer.text: All of: receipt of a Registrar/Inspector report; a special resolution by the company seeking investigation; a request from any Central or State Government department
Receipt of a report from the Registrar or Inspector
A special resolution passed by the company requesting investigation
Request from any Department of Central or State Government

explanation.text: The Logic: Under Section 212(1) of the Companies Act, 2013, the Central Government may assign investigation to SFIO on: receipt of ROC/Inspector report under section 208, a special resolution by the company, in public interest, or on a request from any Central/State Government department. The Trap: Each of these triggers is independently valid — there is no single exclusive trigger. Any one can initiate an SFIO investigation. Distributor's Pro-Tip: SFIO is a multi-disciplinary body under MCA for serious corporate fraud. It has forensic auditing, law, IT, and capital market experts. Know all four investigation triggers.
